title: Practice 3: Rain falls, time flies, luck comes: the idioms

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: А, ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) снег!.
exercises.why: **идет** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. present: я иду́ · ты идёшь · он идёт · мы идём · вы идёте · они иду́т. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **идти**: to go; to walk; (of precipitation) to fall; to function, to work (of clocks and watches).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — Идёт не дождь, а снег. — It's snowing, not raining. · Часы идут. — The clock is ticking. · Идёт фильм. — A film is on. · Это платье тебе идёт. — That dress suits you. · Правительство идёт к демократии. — The government is moving towards democracy.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note the following expressions: Идёт дождь. Фильм идёт. Разговор идёт. Идёт снег. Урок идёт. Работа идёт. Поезд идёт. Дорога идёт. Собрание идёт.» — DLI, Lesson 19.  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Жена».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Время ___ (лететь — to fly, one way) быстро.
exercises.why: **летело** is the past tense (neuter) of **лететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **летать** for many directions. past: он лете́л · она лете́ла · оно лете́ло · они лете́ли. — Wiktionary, «лететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **лететь**: to fly, to be flying.  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лететь — Время летит. — Time flies. · Акции летят от экономического кризиса. — Shares are plummeting because of the economic crisis.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Николай Помяловский, «Мещанское счастье».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Время ___ (бежать — to run, one way) быстро.
exercises.why: **бежит** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **бежать**: (imperfective only) to run, to be running; to flee, to be fleeing; to avoid, to be avoiding, to shun, to be shunning; to run after [with за (za, + instrumental) ‘someone’].  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «бежать — Кровь бежит из раны. — Blood is flowing from the wound. · Дни бегут. — The days fly past.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Гусев».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Совеем не ___ (повезти — to take off (by vehicle))!
exercises.why: **повезло** is the past tense (neuter) of **повезти** (to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport) — the perfective of **везти**, «set out». past: он повёз · она повезла́ · оно повезло́ · они повезли́. — Wiktionary, «повезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **повезти**: to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport; (impersonal) to be lucky, to have luck, to work out for, to succeed, to be successful [with dative ‘for someone’ and infinitive ‘to do something’].  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Общее образование».
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.why: **вели** is the past tense (plural) of **вести** (to lead, to preside over, to chair) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **водить** for many directions. past: он вёл · она вела́ · оно вело́ · они вели́. — Wiktionary, «вести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **вести**: to lead, to preside over, to chair; to drive; to keep.  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «вести — Страна ведёт войну. — The country is waging a war. · Девочка ведёт дневник. — The girl keeps a diary. · Дорога ведёт в город. — The road leads to the city. · Ложь к добру не ведёт. — No good comes from lying.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Лев Толстой, «Отец Сергий».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Некоторое время ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) молча.
exercises.why: **шли** is the past tense (plural) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. past: он шёл · она шла́ · оно шло́ · они шли́. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **идти**: to go; to walk; (of precipitation) to fall; to function, to work (of clocks and watches).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — Идёт не дождь, а снег. — It's snowing, not raining. · Часы идут. — The clock is ticking. · Идёт фильм. — A film is on. · Это платье тебе идёт. — That dress suits you. · Правительство идёт к демократии. — The government is moving towards democracy.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note the following expressions: Идёт дождь. Фильм идёт. Разговор идёт. Идёт снег. Урок идёт. Работа идёт. Поезд идёт. Дорога идёт. Собрание идёт.» — DLI, Lesson 19.  ·  From Максим Горький, «Товарищи».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Однако ему не ___ (везти — to convey by vehicle, one way).
exercises.why: **везло** is the past tense (neuter) of **везти** (to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **возить** for many directions. past: он вёз · она везла́ · оно везло́ · они везли́. — Wiktionary, «везти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **везти**: to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport; (impersonal) to be lucky, to have luck, to work out for, to succeed, to be successful [with dative ‘for someone’ and infinitive ‘to do something’].  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «везти — Ей везёт / повезло. — She is lucky/got lucky.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note also the following idiomatic construction: Мне не везёт. — I am not lucky. Ему везёт. — He is lucky. Вам повезло. — You were lucky.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Александр Беляев, «Человек-амфибия».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Ведь канальское время ___ (бежать — to run, one way), не ждет!
exercises.why: **бежит** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **бежать**: (imperfective only) to run, to be running; to flee, to be fleeing; to avoid, to be avoiding, to shun, to be shunning; to run after [with за (za, + instrumental) ‘someone’].  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «бежать — Кровь бежит из раны. — Blood is flowing from the wound. · Дни бегут. — The days fly past.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Тайный советник».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
